options.how: Scanning wreck fragments unlocks blueprints; you cannot craft an item until you find and scan it.
Items are crafted on a grid, and the recipe book lists what you can make from what you have.

sources.note: Subnautica: underwater survival with scanned blueprints
Minecraft: crafting grid and recipe book

options.how: Most recipes must first be prototyped while standing near a Science Machine or Alchemy Engine; once unlocked they can be crafted anywhere.
The Smithy shows each weapon's forging and upgrade tree, so you can see every next step and what it branches into.

sources.note: Don't Starve: prototype near a Science Machine or Alchemy Engine, then craft anywhere
Monster Hunter: World: Smithy forging tree for weapons and armor

options.how: Recipes are learned through interactions in the facility, and some must also be researched with a minigame before you can craft them.
Most craftable items are known by default; perks such as Science! and Armorer gate what you can build, not recipe hunting.

sources.note: Abiotic Factor: recipes learned via interactions, some need a research minigame
Fallout 4: majority of craftable items known by default, perks required

options.how: Analyzing gathered items at the Resource Analyzer unlocks recipes, and each analysis builds Brainpower that unlocks more.
A Technology list shows blueprints by tier; you spend Technology Points from levels and boss kills to unlock the ones you want.

sources.note: Grounded: analyzing items unlocks recipes and Brainpower
Palworld: blueprints unlocked per tier with Technology Points

options.how: Ore becomes ingots, then plates and screws, then reinforced plates and beyond; each step feeds the next.
Most tools take two or three raw items: an axe is one twig and one flint.

sources.note: Satisfactory: Reinforced Iron Plate from Iron Plates and Screws in an Assembler
Don't Starve: Axe is 1 twig and 1 flint

options.how: A Computer needs Circuit Boards, Bio Batteries, Carbon Fiber and Plasteel, and Circuit Boards in turn need crafted Polymer.
Weapons are forged at the Smithy straight from zenny plus ore or monster materials, with no intermediate parts.

sources.note: Palworld: Circuit Board from Pure Quartz and Polymer, used in Computer
Monster Hunter Wilds: weapons crafted from zenny and materials such as Iron Ore

options.how: Late parts like the Heavy Modular Frame need Modular Frames, Steel Pipes, Encased Industrial Beams and Screws, all crafted components.
Most DIY recipes take raw wood, stone or iron nuggets straight to the finished item at a workbench; only some need a crafted part.

sources.note: Satisfactory: Heavy Modular Frame recipe of intermediate components
Animal Crossing: New Horizons: DIY recipes mostly use raw materials

options.how: Orichalcum Ingots need Starmetal Ingots, which need Steel Ingots, which need Iron Ingots, each step adding flux and charcoal.
Ore and coal are smelted into a bar at a furnace, then hammered into the item at an anvil; higher tiers need no lower bars.

sources.note: New World: Iron, Steel, Starmetal and Orichalcum ingot chain
Old School RuneScape: ore smelted into bars, bars smithed into items

options.how: Crafted gear lands in a Gear Score range set by material and skill, with a chance of extra perks or an empty gem socket.
Recipes list fixed ingredient amounts, such as 3 Grass Planks, 4 Sprigs and 2 Sap, and always produce the same item.

sources.note: New World: Gear Score range by skill and material, chance of perks
Grounded: recipe with fixed ingredient amounts

options.how: Crafting actions raise a Quality bar; the higher it ends, the likelier the item comes out High Quality, and HQ inputs start it higher.
Each weapon has fixed attack, affinity and rarity; forging it from zenny and monster parts always gives the same stats.

sources.note: Final Fantasy XIV: Quality sets the chance of a High Quality result
Monster Hunter Rise: weapon table with fixed stats and crafting costs

options.how: Forged weapons are rated on your smithing performance and come in quality tiers; potions get better with precise brewing.
Every weapon in the forging tree has listed attack, affinity and rarity; forging it always yields exactly those stats.

sources.note: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II: performance rating and weapon quality tiers
Kingdom Come: Deliverance II: following the recipe evenly gives masterful potions
Monster Hunter: World: weapon table with fixed attack, affinity and rarity

options.how: Crafted items get quality grades from fine up to masterwork, set mainly by the crafter's skill and the materials used.
Each weapon has fixed attack, affinity and rarity values; crafting it from zenny and materials always gives the same weapon.

sources.note: Dwarf Fortress: quality grades set by creator skill and materials
Monster Hunter Wilds: weapon table with fixed stats and crafting costs

options.how: Buildings can be placed anywhere at any angle, and homes fill burgage plots drawn around your roads and the terrain.
Buildings snap to tile cells with fixed footprints, such as the 2x2 Manual Generator, inside a grid of 1x1 tiles.

sources.note: Manor Lords: full freedom of placement and rotation, burgage plots
Oxygen Not Included: Manual Generator is 2x2 tiles

options.how: Gridless: you paint zones and assemble modular buildings from parts, with almost no construction constraints.
Everything sits on a tile grid: 1x1 tiles form walls, floors and ceilings, and machines take fixed footprints like 2x2.

sources.note: Foundation: gridless medieval city builder with modular buildings
Oxygen Not Included: 1x1 tiles are the basic building block
Oxygen Not Included: Manual Generator is 2x2 tiles

options.how: Gridless: you drag walls and paths freely and the game generates stonework to fit.
You click cells on an irregular grid and each fills with a block that adapts to its neighbors.

sources.note: Tiny Glade: gridless free-form building with no goals
Townscaper: irregular grid, no goal

options.how: Gridless: buildings go anywhere at any rotation, and burgage plots subdivide to fit your roads and the land.
The world is built of 1x1 voxel blocks; terrain blocks and constructions are placed block by block and stacked in layers.

sources.note: Manor Lords: gridless city building with free placement and rotation
Timberborn: 1x1 cubic voxel blocks, stacking and overhang rules

options.how: Each piece shows its support by color, blue to red; build too far from the ground and pieces break.
Settlement pieces snap together without structural load; floors and walls hold wherever they snap.

sources.note: Valheim: structural integrity building and rewarding food
Fallout 4: settlement building

options.how: Blocks carry load and need support; unsupported blocks fall, so damage can collapse a base.
Most blocks ignore gravity, so you can build floating platforms and houses anywhere.

sources.note: 7 Days to Die: unsupported blocks fall
Terraria: most blocks are not affected by gravity

options.how: Constructions or ground detached from all support cave in, crashing down and destroying buildings underneath.
Pieces need no load support; only the C.A.M.P. budget and no-build zones limit where and how much you build.

sources.note: Dwarf Fortress: unsupported constructions and terrain cave in
Fallout 76: C.A.M.P. limited by budget and placement rules, structures can float on stairs

options.how: Terrain blocks can reach at most three blocks sideways or overhang three blocks past a fully supported block.
C.A.M.P. building is capped by a budget and placement rules, with no structural load; builds can even float above terrain on stairs.

sources.note: Timberborn: side placement and overhang limited to three blocks
Fallout 76: C.A.M.P. limited by budget and placement rules, structures can float on stairs

options.how: Furniture, flowers and trees raise the island star rating for development and scenery; nothing you place defends you.
Walls, gates and towers keep swarms of thousands of infected out of the colony.

sources.note: Animal Crossing: New Horizons: star rating from development and scenery
They Are Billions: build walls, gates and towers against the infected

options.how: No goal and no resources: you plop colored blocks on an irregular grid purely for how the town looks.
You design a castle with gates and killing zones; its layout decides whether you hold off enemy attacks and sieges.

sources.note: Townscaper: no goal, colored blocks on an irregular grid
Stronghold: build a castle with killing zones and hold off attacks

options.how: Castles and cottages are pure expression; nothing attacks and no building has a stat.
Walls and towers you pay for stand between your town and the Greed attacking each night.

sources.note: Tiny Glade: gridless free-form building with no goals
Kingdom Two Crowns: Greed attack at night; walls and towers defend

options.how: Decor customizes your Housing Plot, up to 3,500 pieces, and has no gameplay effect beyond how your home looks.
Every 7th night a Blood Moon horde breaks down obstacles to reach you, so bases must be built to withstand it.

sources.note: Palia: decor customizes the Housing Plot, no gameplay effects
7 Days to Die: horde every 7th day breaks obstacles to reach the player

options.how: Player housing lets you furnish and decorate a house or apartment as a social showcase.
Enclosed rooms that match a room recipe, like a kitchen or bedroom, gain functions residents use.

sources.note: Final Fantasy XIV: quality raises the chance of an HQ item
Dragon Quest Builders 2: block building RPG

options.how: You repair and remodel one house at a time: walls, floors, paint and furniture inside each room.
You lay out a whole city of districts, road networks, utilities and services.

sources.note: House Flipper: buy, repair and remodel houses
Cities: Skylines: city builder about zoning, services and traffic

options.how: You fit out rooms inside one hospital building, sizing each and placing desks, beds and machines.
You plan an entire Roman city: housing blocks, roads, aqueducts, farms, temples and walls.

sources.note: Theme Hospital: design and manage a hospital from an empty building
Caesar III: a governor career of city missions pleasing the emperor

options.how: Building centers on your own home plot: rooms, walls and furniture for one house.
You place whole towns of buildings across a procedurally generated island.

sources.note: Palia: home plot with building blocks and decor
Islanders: relaxing builder, placing buildings rewarded with points

options.how: You build and run one maximum security prison, laying out holding cells, canteen, infirmary and guard room yourself.
You create huge metropolises, settle a new continent and link them with numerous production chains.

sources.note: Prison Architect: build and manage one maximum security prison
Anno 1800: huge metropolises, a new continent and production chains

options.how: Calories, thirst, fatigue and warmth all drain; let them empty and you die, permanently in Survival mode.
No starvation: up to three foods at once temporarily raise max health and stamina.

sources.note: The Long Dark: calories, thirst, fatigue, cold, wolves; permadeath in Survival
Valheim: structural integrity building and rewarding food

options.how: When hunger or thirst runs low a countdown appears; let it run out and you instantly perish.
Food grants Well Fed or stronger tiers for defense, damage and speed; hunger only matters in special seeds like The Constant.

sources.note: Abiotic Factor: hunger or thirst countdown ends in instant death
Terraria: Well Fed buffs, hunger only in special seeds

options.how: You track food, water, health and stamina, and must keep yourself and your villagers from starving or dying of thirst.
Up to three food slots give timed bonuses to health, stamina or damage by food type; skipping meals only forgoes the bonus.

sources.note: Medieval Dynasty: monitor food, water, health, do not starve or die of thirst
Enshrouded: three food slots with timed buffs

options.how: When Hunger hits zero, Health drains at 1.25 per second until you eat something or die.
Eating Bunny Dango at the Tea Shop boosts max Health and Stamina and can trigger dango skills for the quest.

sources.note: Don't Starve Together: starvation drains Health until you eat or die
Monster Hunter Rise: Bunny Dango boost max Health and Stamina, dango skills

options.how: Relaxed mode keeps the full game with far less survival upkeep, and life support or hazard drain can be slowed or switched off.
Hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold drain you while wolves and bears hunt you; in Survival, death deletes your save.

sources.note: No Man's Sky: Relaxed mode and adjustable life support and hazard drain
The Long Dark: hunger, thirst, fatigue, cold, wildlife, save deleted on death

options.how: Thirst, oxygen and temperature need upkeep, but there are no enemies and a chill difficulty keeps survival light.
Slavers, cannibals, wild beasts and famine threaten you everywhere, and wounded squad mates must be carried home alive.

sources.note: The Planet Crafter: thirst, oxygen, temperature; chill to hardcore; no violence
Kenshi: slavers, cannibals, wild beasts and famine

options.how: Food slots only add timed bonuses, with no penalty listed for an empty stomach, so upkeep never threatens you.
Hunger, thirst, illness and depression pile on in a zombie-infested sandbox built around one question: how will you die?

sources.note: Enshrouded: food gives timed buffs only
Project Zomboid: hunger, thirst and illness, how will you die

options.how: Survival upkeep is a setting: Relaxed lightens it, and life support or hazard protection drain can be slowed or turned off.
Starvation and winter freezing each drain 1.25 Health per second until you eat, warm up or die.

sources.note: No Man's Sky: Relaxed mode, adjustable life support and hazard drain
Don't Starve Together: freezing deals 1.25 damage per second
Don't Starve Together: starvation drains Health until you eat or die
